item.content:encoded:
The Russians are launching an attack along the border with Poland. Day 1665 of the war

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-09-19

Reports of Russian forces withdrawing to the Zherebets River line north of Lyman have been confirmed. This has eliminated the encirclement of Sloviansk from the north and has relatively levelled the front line. Most of the territory of the former breach has returned to Ukrainian control, though the Russians still maintain a broad bridgehead on the western bank of the river. According to some sources, the defenders also managed to carry out a series of successful counterattacks in the north-eastern part of Kharkiv Oblast, thereby averting the threat of their forces being encircled.

The Russians have captured part of the territory between the breaches made so far west of Pokrovsk, east of Dobropillia and west of Kostiantynivka, thereby limiting the potential threat posed by Ukrainian counterattacks. The flanking of Druzhkivka has intensified, whilst the invading forces have not achieved much success in Dobropillia or in Mykolaivka, which borders Sloviansk to the east. On 11 September, Russian guided aerial bombs destroyed the railway bridge connecting the eastern and western parts of Sloviansk (the road bridges had previously been destroyed).

Russian forces have entered the centre of Orikhiv, which is currently the scene of fighting. According to some sources, Mala Tokmachka, which neighbours Orikhiv to the east, has also come under their control. item.title: [19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland] US sanctions bill on Russia: a political tool with uncertain prospects for implementation
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
US sanctions bill on Russia: a political tool with uncertain prospects for implementation

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-09-19

On 16 September, the US House of Representatives passed a bill imposing sanctions on Russia, originally proposed by the late Senator Lindsey Graham. The vote completed the bill’s passage through Congress, and it now awaits the president’s signature. The legislation restates existing visa and asset restrictions imposed under presidential executive orders, which target senior Russian state officials as well as Russian and foreign entities supporting Moscow’s war effort. It also grants the US president broad powers to impose tariffs on Russia and on countries importing Russian energy resources (see Appendix).

Congress’s passage of the bill should be viewed primarily as a political signal and a potential instrument of US pressure on Russia, intended to induce the Kremlin to engage meaningfully in negotiations on ending the war with Ukraine. However, the broad discretion the legislation gives the presidential administration over how sanctions are implemented weakens the force of this political message in the Kremlin’s eyes, given the White House’s perceived reluctance to expand restrictions that could drive up fuel prices.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Further disruption to Middle Eastern oil supplies

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-09-19

On 10 September, following attacks by Iran-aligned forces and damage to infrastructure, Saudi Aramco shut down the East-West pipeline. On 15 September, reports emerged that a number of crude oil deliveries to European refineries scheduled for late September had been cancelled or postponed. As a result, the most important route for transporting crude oil from the Persian Gulf as an alternative to the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran has blocked since March, has temporarily ceased to operate. This is further exacerbating an already significant global oil supply disruption. European buyers of Saudi crude, including Poland’s Orlen, are among those affected and must replace the lost supplies at short notice.

The situation in the Middle East has driven further increases in oil prices. On 15 September, Brent crude futures rose above $109 per barrel, while physical North Sea crude cargoes traded at more than $137 per barrel that day. This is also affecting petroleum products markets worldwide, particularly diesel prices in Europe. The supply shock, now in its seventh month, combined with the lack of any clear prospect of ending the war in the Persian Gulf or even of reaching a political settlement that would allow the full resumption of oil exports from the region, is increasing the risk of a deepening oil crisis across global markets, including in Europe.
